findings.claim: SCP-R-002 allow fixture corpus covers only the rule_id identity path; the finding_id-scoped allow case has no testdata fixture, leaving the AC-2 'rule_id OR finding_id' allow surface uncovered in the conftest self-test harness.
findings.evidence: policies/testdata/SCP-R-002/allow/waivers.json (line 7) contains a single entry with rule_id:SCP-R-001 and no finding_id. scp_r_002_test.rego:25-35 (test_scp_r_002_allows_finding_scoped_waiver) covers the finding_id allow path in OPA unit tests, but the testdata tree has no corresponding fixture. The conftest self-test harness exercises testdata fixtures directly; if the finding_id branch of scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload is removed or broken in a future refactor, the OPA test catches it but the fixture-driven conftest path does not.
findings.impact: Incomplete fixture documentation of the valid-waiver shape surface for SCP-R-002. A regression in the finding_id branch would be invisible to any fixture-based integration test. The AC-4 fixture pair requirement is structurally met (allow/ and deny/ both exist) but semantically incomplete relative to the two-identity-field contract in AC-2.
findings.mitigation: Add policies/testdata/SCP-R-002/allow/waivers_finding_scoped.json containing [{"approved_by":"@jrnb2024","created_at":"2026-04-28","expires_at":"2099-09-30","reason":"Finding-scoped allow fixture","finding_id":"F-SVC-003-area-service-signal"}]. No rule_id field. This exercises the scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload finding_id branch through the conftest path as well as the unit-test path.

findings.claim: The 'Emit disabled-rule observability records' step in policy-check.yml emits SCP-E006 entries (including the no-manifest-applicable record written by the preceding step) as ::error annotations, which is semantically incorrect for a non-blocking informational signal.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:557 — print(f"::error file={config_path},title=SCP-E006::{rule_id} disabled: {reason}; expires_at={expires_at}"). The preceding step ('Emit SCP-R-003 no-manifest observability record', policy-check.yml:401-423) appends {rule_id:SCP-R-003, reason:no-manifest-applicable, expires_at:2099-12-31} to disabled-rules.json unconditionally whenever no manifest file is in the PR diff. The 'Emit disabled-rule observability records' step then reads this entry and emits it as ::error. AC-3 in dispatch-package.json describes SCP-E006 as an 'observability record' that is explicitly non-blocking.
findings.impact: On any repository whose PR diff contains no package.json, pyproject.toml, or go.mod files (the expected case for many non-manifest repos in the estate), every policy-check run will produce a red ::error annotation in the GitHub PR UI for SCP-E006. This trains engineers to ignore ::error annotations from the SCP workflow, which degrades the signal fidelity of genuine SCP-E003 deny annotations. The false alarm rate is proportional to the number of non-manifest PRs in the estate.
findings.mitigation: Change the SCP-E006 annotation emission in policy-check.yml:557 from ::error to ::notice. Alternatively gate on reason: emit ::error only for genuinely operator-disabled rules (reason != 'no-manifest-applicable') and ::notice for the no-manifest observability case. Owned by the 020B slice; carry as a 020C.1 or 020C.2 tracked-forward item with a named owner in the next slice dispatch.

findings.claim: README.md step 6 prescribes aggregate 'opa test policies/ -v --coverage' for local verification, but the fr1 'Enforce per-rule OPA coverage' CI step enforces the ≥90% threshold rule-by-rule in isolation. A contributor who passes the README command locally can still fail CI if one individual rule falls below 90% while aggregate coverage compensates.
findings.evidence: policies/README.md:60 (step 6) — 'opa test policies/ -v --coverage'. policy-check.yml:385-393 (Enforce per-rule OPA coverage step) — runs 'opa test "${rule_file}" "${test_file}" --coverage --threshold 90 --fail-on-empty -v' per rule individually. OPA's --threshold flag applies to the aggregate coverage of all files passed to that invocation: running all rules together produces a combined coverage metric, not per-rule coverage. If R-001 is at 85% and R-002 is at 98%, the aggregate exceeds 90% and the README command passes; the CI gate fails because R-001 is measured in isolation.
findings.impact: The AC-6 contributing guide (step 6) gives developers a local verification command that does not faithfully reproduce the CI enforcement mode introduced by the fr1 CG-001 fix. A contributor can arrive at a CI failure that their local run did not predict, eroding trust in the contributing guide. This is a new discrepancy created by fr1.
findings.mitigation: Update policies/README.md step 6 to replace 'opa test policies/ -v --coverage' with the per-rule loop matching CI: 'for rule_file in policies/SCP-R-*.rego; do rule_base=$(basename $rule_file .rego); test_file=policies/tests/$(printf "%s" $rule_base | tr "[:upper:]-" "[:lower:]_")_test.rego; opa test $rule_file $test_file --coverage --threshold 90 --fail-on-empty -v; done'. A one-liner code block in the checklist is sufficient.

findings.claim: README.md fixture template names both fixture files input.yml, diverging from the established per-rule convention of domain-named files (services.yml, waivers.json) and variant-named subdirectories (package_json/input.yml).
findings.evidence: policies/README.md:38-51 — fixture template shows 'policies/testdata/SCP-R-NNN/allow/input.yml' and 'policies/testdata/SCP-R-NNN/deny/input.yml'. Actual conventions: SCP-R-001 uses allow/services.yml and deny/services.yml; SCP-R-002 uses allow/waivers.json and deny/waivers.json; SCP-R-003 uses variant subdirectories (allow/package_json/input.yml, deny/go_mod/input.yml). All three patterns diverge from the template's flat input.yml.
findings.impact: A contributor copying the template verbatim names their fixture input.yml. The file is functionally accepted by conftest (it loads any YAML/JSON), but the name makes the fixture tree harder to scan, diverges from established convention, and provides no signal about which input file the rule validates. Low blast radius; caught at code review.
findings.mitigation: Update the README fixture template comment lines to read '# policies/testdata/SCP-R-NNN/allow/<file-being-validated>.{yml,json}' and add one sentence: 'Name the fixture after the target file (e.g., services.yml, waivers.json) or after the input variant (e.g., package_json/input.yml) to aid triage.'
